chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: Stopping in Kansas City, the Reno Club and Bill Hadnot
summary: On a layover he walked into the Reno Club, where bassist Bill Hadnot, an old Tulsa friend, was playing with Bus Moten's band and gave him his room.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, what did you think you were going to do then? You'd got an uncle, but --
Well, I had an uncle there and the biggest thing I was interested in was somewhere to stay. So I figured I could get something to do, as long as I had somewhere to stay.
But you didn't get there.

But I didn't get to Omaha. I had to change buses in Kansas City. So I decided, I said, "Well, I'm going --" I had an hour layover in Kansas City. So I says, "I'm going to go up here to this Reno Club and see what they doing up there." So I walked in, when I walked in the door, Bill Hadnot was playing bass with --
Yeah. Bill went to the West Coast.
Yes, yes. And he was playing bass with Bus Moten Band. See, Basie's gone East already, see?
Oh, this was --
Basie's Band was -- left Kansas City.
Is that '37 then? Is that '37?
Right, '37.
Did you hear them?
I never heard Basie until after he came back from East.
Is that right?
That's right. I never heard Basie's band.
Well, Bus Moten was playing piano,

Bus was playing piano and he had a guy named Popeye on the sax, Luther West and Jesse Price and Had not was on bass, Squonch Hall was on trumpet and Dee Stewart was on trumpet and when I came in, Had not recognized me right away.
Where had you met him?
Well, I'd met him in Tulsa, when I was playing with Al Dennie's band. And he left Tulsa with Andy Kirk.
Oh.

He didn't have a bass. I'm sure it was Andy Kirk that he left with. But if it wasn't Andy, he left with a show and joined Andy later. But I know that the thing was, he went with Andy. I know that. That was the big thing, you know. And --
Why did you say he didn't have a bass?
Well, he didn't have a bass in Tulsa and whoever he left with got him a bass.
You mean, he was playing bass, but he didn't own one.
He was playing bass, but he didn't own a bass.
What did he do then, rent one?
How's that?
What did he do, rent a bass or borrow one?
Well, you know how guys borrow a bass, borrow a this or that, you know?
Yeah.

And -- because he told me, you know, that they bought him a bass, you know, and then he told me, he says, "Hey, Mack, what are you doing in town?" I says, "Well, I'm on my way to Omaha. The gig played out down here in Kansas. I got an uncle in Omaha and I'm going to go up there and see what's happening." He said, "No, you don't want to go no further. You stay right here in Kansas City." I said, "Man, I don't have no money." He said, "Well, you stay out to my room. Take my room."
Wasn't that nice.

I said, "Well, where are you going to stay?" He says, "Well, I got a girlfriend here. I'll stay out to her pad." You know what I mean? "Don't worry about a place. You can have my place." So I says, "Well, okay." And so he says, "Wait until I get off and we'll go by and get your things at the bus station." So that's what we did.
Wasn't that nice.
It hit just perfect and so he says, "You'll be able to get a gig in town. So don't be worrying
